name: Advances and Challenges in Foundation Agents: From Brain-Inspired Intelligence to Evolutionary, Collaborative, and Safe Systems (Foundation Agents Survey / Liu et al.)
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2504.01990, cs.AI). Submitted 31 Mar 2025 (v1), last revised 2 Aug 2025 (v2). A large multi-institution survey / 'book'-length report (~264 pages, ~1,416 references per the authors); not (as of writing) a peer-reviewed conference/journal paper, though the title was also presented as Keynote 3 at SANER 2025. No formally published peer-reviewed venue confirmed [uncertain].

Chi Wang, Jian Pei (corresponding; Duke University), Qiang Yang (corresponding; HKUST), Xiaoliang Qi (corresponding; Stanford University), Chenglin Wu (corresponding; DeepWisdom / MetaGPT) -- 48 authors total. code_url: https://github.com/FoundationAgents/awesome-foundation-agents (curated paper/repo/blog list accompanying the survey; not a runnable method implementation since this is a survey).
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/FoundationAgents/awesome-foundation-agents (continuously-updated GitHub 'awesome' list maintained by the authors / MetaGPT community; description: 'Awesome things towards foundation agents. Papers / Repos / Blogs / ...'; created Mar 2025, ~2.1k+ stars, more current than the frozen PDF).
task_domain: Survey / taxonomy. Broad, book-length survey of LLM-based / foundation agents organized around a modular brain-inspired architecture; spans reasoning, perception, memory, world modeling, reward, emotion, action/tool-use, self-evolution/optimization, multi-agent collaboration, and AI safety, rather than a single task domain.
problem_setting: This is a comprehensive literature survey (a ~264-page report with ~1,416 references), not a method/system with experiments. It frames intelligent agents within a modular, brain-inspired architecture integrating principles from cognitive science, neuroscience, and computational research, and is structured into four interconnected parts: (1) the modular foundation of intelligent agents -- mapping cognitive, perceptual, and operational modules onto analogous human-brain functionalities and elucidating core components such as memory, world modeling, reward processing, goal, and emotion; (2) self-enhancement and adaptive evolution -- how agents autonomously refine capabilities, adapt to dynamic environments, and achieve continual learning via automated optimization (incl. AutoML- and LLM-driven optimization); (3) collaborative and evolutionary multi-agent systems -- collective intelligence from agent interaction, cooperation, and societal structures; and (4) safe and beneficial AI -- intrinsic/extrinsic security threats, ethical alignment, robustness, and mitigation. It covers both offline and interactive, and single- and multi-agent settings as surveyed sub-areas, but defines no controlled experimental protocol, supervision, or benchmark of its own.
what_is_retrieved: N/A for the survey as an artifact (it does not itself retrieve). As surveyed topics it covers agent memory retrieval (retrieving past experiences/observations/dialogue from episodic/long-term memory), tool/skill retrieval and use, and retrieval of external knowledge; within the brain-inspired taxonomy, 'memory' is an explicit module the agent reads from and writes to.
retrieval_grounding: Survey-level: covers BOTH a GROWING/episodic agent memory (the surveyed memory module that agents write to and later retrieve from, central to self-evolution/continual learning) and access to STATIC external knowledge/tools/APIs. The survey itself is not grounded in any single corpus.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: N/A (survey, no retrieval objective of its own). Surveyed memory retrieval is generally described as similarity/score-based top-k recall rather than a completeness or precision-driven variable-size objective; the survey does not standardize an objective.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (the survey is not a case-based-reasoning system; it implements no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain cycle). It does survey experience reuse, self-reflection, and memory-update mechanisms in cited agents, which loosely parallel CBR phases, but provides no CBR cycle of its own.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The survey does not frame foundation agents as case-based reasoning and does not center Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it organizes the field around a brain-inspired modular framework (memory, world model, reward, goal, emotion, perception, action, plus self-evolution / multi-agent / safety).
retrieval_unit: N/A (survey defines no retrieval unit of its own). Surveyed units span memory entries (past interactions/observations/experiences), distilled skills/workflows, tool/API descriptions, and external documents/knowledge; the survey reviews this spectrum within its memory and action/tool modules rather than fixing a unit.
index_source: N/A for the survey. Surveyed agent memory is a growing store written online/at test time (episodic/long-term memory enabling continual learning and self-evolution), while tool/knowledge access is from static external resources; the survey builds no index itself.
index_structure_topology: N/A (survey has no index of its own). It reviews memory representations and substrates used by agents -- e.g., natural-language/in-context memory, vector/embedding stores, and structured/graph-based knowledge (knowledge graphs) -- thus surveying both flat and structured/graph organizations rather than prescribing one.
retriever_type: N/A (survey; no retriever implemented). Surveyed memory retrieval methods include embedding/similarity (dense) retrieval and heuristic scoring; tool/skill selection is often LLM-driven; the survey catalogs these rather than implementing one.
retriever_learning_signal: N/A (survey; no retriever is trained). It surveys agents whose memory/skill selection ranges from off-the-shelf similarity to feedback- and reflection-driven and (in self-evolution sections) learned/optimized selection, but contributes no trained retriever of its own.
query_construction: N/A (survey). For surveyed memory retrieval the current state/observation/task acts as the query matched against stored memories; the survey proposes no query-construction method itself.
query_granularity: N/A (survey). Surveyed agents retrieve from memory at the step/state level during interaction and at the task level for skill/experience reuse; the survey prescribes no single granularity.
when_to_retrieve: N/A (survey). Surveyed memory/skill retrieval occurs interactively (when the agent needs relevant content during reasoning/decision-making) and is largely agent-initiated; the survey does not standardize a trigger.
retrieval_trigger_signal: N/A (survey defines no trigger). Surveyed agent-initiated retrieval is driven by the agent's need for relevant memory/skills during decision-making (agent-initiated / per-step), within reasoning loops; the survey contributes no concrete trigger signal.
reranking: N/A (survey; no reranking stage of its own). Surveyed memory selection may use relevance/recency/importance-style scoring as a ranking heuristic in cited systems, but the survey proposes no reranker.
retrieved_context_refinement: N/A (survey). It discusses memory operations such as reflection, summarization/abstraction, and consolidation in surveyed systems (and learning to distill experiences into skills/workflows in the self-evolution part) as post-storage processing, but proposes no refinement pipeline itself.
tool_document_engineering: N/A as a method contribution. The survey reviews tool-use/action modules (tool selection, tool creation, tool/skill libraries) and how agents consult tool descriptions/demonstrations, but does not propose its own tool-document-engineering technique.
index_content_separation: N/A (survey; no index-vs-content separation mechanism of its own).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (survey). It surveys tool/action use and tool creation/learning at a high level and touches on agent ecosystems/protocols, but does not center a live-synchronized tool index or a specific integration protocol (e.g., MCP) as a contribution.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (survey). It discusses tool/action modules, tool creation, and tool/skill composition at a high level but does not center an inter-tool dependency-graph retrieval formalism of its own.
how_retrieved_used: N/A as a method. The survey describes how agents use retrieved/recalled content: prompt/context augmentation (recalled memory, skills, and tool descriptions placed in context to inform reasoning, planning, and action), skill/experience reuse, tool invocation, and reflection; in self-evolution sections, retrieved experience also serves as a signal for self-improvement/optimization. The survey implements none of these.
planning_integration: N/A as a method. The survey reviews reasoning, planning, and action as brain-inspired operational modules and surveys planning/decision paradigms (decomposition, search/tree-style reasoning, feedback-driven planning, world-model-based planning) and how memory/tools interface with them, but proposes no single integration.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: N/A (survey). It contrasts one-shot vs interleaved/per-step reasoning-and-acting paradigms (e.g., decompose-first vs ReAct-style per-step) as surveyed approaches rather than committing to one interleaving granularity.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not a CBR method; no retrieved-case adaptation mechanism of its own). In the self-evolution part it does survey how agents adapt/refine reused experiences via reflection, execution feedback, and automated optimization, but contributes no adaptation mechanism itself.
retrieved_item_representation: N/A (survey). Surveyed memory/knowledge is represented as natural-language entries, structured notes/graphs, or distilled skills/workflows; the survey injects nothing itself but reviews this range across its memory and self-evolution sections.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: N/A (survey). Surveyed memory ranges from raw interaction/observation traces to distilled reflections, reusable skills, and procedural workflows (a spectrum it explicitly discusses in the memory and self-evolution parts) rather than a single fixed abstraction level.
noise_robustness_mechanism: N/A (survey). It discusses self-reflection, verification/critique, and (in the safety part) robustness against adversarial/erroneous inputs in surveyed systems, but contributes no specific retrieval-noise-robustness mechanism.
memory_type: Survey-level: 'memory' is an explicit core module in the brain-inspired taxonomy. The survey reviews short-term/working (in-context) and long-term memory, episodic memory, semantic/procedural memory, skill libraries, and graph-structured memory, and treats memory as central to continual learning and self-evolution. As an artifact the survey itself has no memory.
write_back: N/A as a method. Surveyed agents DO write back experiences/skills/knowledge into memory; the survey covers memory writing/reading/reflection/consolidation as core operations and ties memory growth to self-evolution, but the survey itself stores nothing.
online_growth: N/A as a method. Surveyed agent memory grows online during interaction/deployment (continually storing new experiences to enable continual learning and self-evolution); the survey itself has no growing store.
write_back_trigger: N/A (survey; no write-back trigger of its own). Surveyed memory writing is generally per-interaction/per-step, with reflective consolidation/summarization (after self-critique) and, in some cited systems, success/failure-conditioned storage; the survey does not standardize a trigger.
failure_experience_usage: N/A (survey). It discusses agents learning from environmental feedback and self-reflection (using both success and failure signals, e.g., Reflexion-style verbal reinforcement and experiential learning surveyed in the self-evolution part), but contributes no specific failure-experience storage scheme.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (survey). It surveys post-write memory dynamics in cited systems -- consolidation, summarization/abstraction, reflection-based updating, forgetting/pruning -- as part of the memory and self-evolution discussion, but proposes no single update policy.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: N/A (survey). Surveyed memory retrieval is largely heuristic/similarity-based; while the self-evolution part surveys learned/optimized agent behaviors (incl. RL- and LLM-driven optimization), the survey does not center retrieval-as-a-learned-policy as its own contribution.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Surveyed (not a method contribution): a major part of the survey covers collaborative and evolutionary multi-agent systems -- agent interaction, cooperation, communication, societal structures, and collective intelligence -- which include shared/collective memory and experience across multiple agents; it reviews rather than implements cross-agent sharing.
benchmarks: N/A (survey; runs no experiments and reports no benchmark results of its own). It references and discusses many agent benchmarks/environments used by surveyed works across reasoning, embodied, web, tool-use, code, memory, multi-agent, and safety areas, but presents no controlled evaluation.
benchmark_family: N/A (survey). Surveyed sub-areas span QA/reasoning, web, embodied, tool, code, memory, multi-agent, and safety benchmark families, but the survey itself reports no benchmark-family results.
baselines: N/A (survey; no method comparison or baselines of its own).
key_metrics: N/A (survey; reports no quantitative metrics of its own).
headline_result: N/A (survey; no headline number). Its 'headline' contribution is the modular, brain-inspired foundation-agent framework (mapping memory, world modeling, reward, goal, emotion, perception, action onto brain functionalities) plus a comprehensive synthesis spanning self-evolution, multi-agent collaboration, and safety, organized across ~264 pages and ~1,416 references from ~20 institutions; ~138 citations on Semantic Scholar as of mid-2025 and ranked #1 Paper of the Day on Hugging Face at release.
ablations: N/A (survey; no ablations). As a literature survey it conducts no experiments and therefore reports no component ablations.
evaluation_decoupling: N/A (survey reports no retrieval or end-to-end metrics). It discusses agent evaluation as a research topic but performs no intrinsic-vs-end-to-end metric decoupling.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: N/A (survey; performs no scoring). It discusses, at the field level, evaluation dimensions for agents (capabilities, behaviors, safety) but does not itself score process or outcome.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: N/A (survey; no cost/efficiency measurements of its own). Efficiency, scalability, and cost of agents/multi-agent systems appear only as general discussion/challenge topics.
context_budget_and_selection_count: N/A (survey; no token budget or k of its own). It discusses limited context windows and the role of memory in extending effective context as a surveyed challenge.
survey_scope_and_axes: Primary organizing axes: a four-part structure built on a modular, brain-inspired AI-agent framework. Part I -- Core components of intelligent agents: cognition/reasoning, perception, action/tool-use, memory, world model, reward, goal, emotion (mapped onto human-brain functionalities). Part II -- Self-enhancement and adaptive evolution: autonomous capability refinement, continual learning, and automated optimization (incl. AutoML and LLM-driven optimization). Part III -- Collaborative and evolutionary multi-agent systems: agent interaction, cooperation, communication, societal structures, collective intelligence. Part IV -- Safe and beneficial AI: intrinsic/extrinsic security threats, ethical alignment, robustness, mitigation. Coverage: through ~early-mid 2025 (v1 Mar 2025, v2 Aug 2025). Scale: ~264 pages, ~1,416 references, 48 authors across ~20 institutions, coordinated via the MetaGPT community.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (this is a survey, not a benchmark; it constructs no dataset and reports no dataset size or best-system score of its own).
builds_on: Builds conceptually on the foundation-model / LLM-agent literature and on cognitive science / neuroscience analogies; synthesizes prior work on agent reasoning and planning (CoT, ReAct, Tree-of-Thoughts-style search, RL fine-tuning such as ReFT, Search-R1, RAGEN), memory (episodic/long-term/skill-library/graph memory), tool-use and skill learning (e.g., Voyager-style skill libraries), experiential learning and reflection (Reflexion, ExpeL, Self-Refine, AutoManual), world models, multi-agent systems (notably MetaGPT and related frameworks), automated optimization/AutoML, and AI safety/alignment. It aggregates and organizes these as a survey rather than extending a single predecessor method.
contrasts_with: Positions itself as a more brain-inspired, modular, and interdisciplinary synthesis than prior LLM-agent surveys, and against narrower single-capability or single-framework treatments; complements contemporaneous broad LLM-agent surveys (e.g., Xi et al. 'The Rise and Potential of LLM-Based Agents' brain/perception/action survey, and 'Large Language Model Agent: A Survey on Methodology, Applications and Challenges') by emphasizing the cognitive-science/neuroscience mapping plus self-evolution and safety.
lineage: Surveys group: a broad, book-length 2025 foundation-agent survey providing a brain-inspired modular taxonomy (memory, world model, reward, goal, emotion, perception, action) plus self-evolution, multi-agent collaboration, and safety. It is an umbrella reference for the agent-memory, planning/reasoning, tool-use, and self-evolution sub-topics that the retrieval-augmented-agent lineage (Groups A-F) specializes, rather than a method within any single sub-topic.
